# Additions to Esther Chapter 4 (Addition D) — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Additions to Esther D | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/ADE_004_page_001.jpg

---

*[Addition D: Esther's audience with the king. This greatly expands Hebrew Esther 5:1-2. God directly intervenes to transform the king's wrath into gentleness.]*

**1** On the third day, when she had finished praying, she removed her mourning garments and put on her splendid attire.

**2** Resplendent and radiant, calling upon God the overseer and savior of all, she took two maidservants with her.

**3** On one she leaned, as though luxuriating in her softness, while the other followed after, carrying her train.

**4** She was radiant with the beauty of her appearance, and her face was glad as one beloved — yet her heart was in anguish because of fear.

**5** Having passed through all the doors, she stood before the king. He was seated on his royal throne, clothed in the full splendor of his majesty — gold and precious stones — and he was terrifying to behold.

**6** Lifting his face, flushed with glory, he looked at her with fury. The queen faltered; she turned pale, and bowing forward she rested her head on the shoulder of the maidservant who walked before her.

**7** Then God changed the spirit of the king to gentleness. In alarm he leaped from his throne and caught her in his arms until she came to herself, and he reassured her with words of peace. He said to her:

**8** "What is the matter, Esther? I am your brother. Take courage!

**9** You will not die, for our decree applies only to the common people. Come near."

**10** And raising the golden scepter, he laid it on her neck and embraced her, and said:

**11** "Speak to me."

**12** And she said to him: "I saw you, my lord, as an angel of God, and my heart was troubled because of the awe of your glory.

**13** For you are wonderful, my lord, and your face is full of grace."

**14** And as she was speaking, she fainted and collapsed; and the king was distressed, and all his servants worked to revive her.
